text: **dsh-language-guard**（DSH 网页插件）：为推理、回复和工具调用描述加入指定语言约束。它在系统提示词首尾及强化档的中段注册约束文本，并提供自动或手动语言选择、B/C/D 三档强度、保留代码术语、自定义规则、周期提醒、设置卡片、侧栏快速切换和 `/language` 临时命令。适合希望 DSH 持续使用指定语言工作的用户；无需额外 API 密钥。

**dsh-language-guard** (DSH web plugin) adds chosen-language rules to system prompts. It supports automatic or manual language selection, three strength levels, custom rules, periodic reminders, a settings card, sidebar switching, and a temporary `/language` command. No API key is needed.
让 DSH 的推理和回复始终使用我指定的语言。
我想让语言约束出现在系统提示词的多个位置。
能否让 DSH 自动跟随界面语言来回复？
想临时把当前会话切换成日语，不改保存的设置。
Keep the assistant reasoning and responding in a chosen language.
Can the target language follow the app interface automatically?
Switch the current session language without changing saved settings.
Remind the model periodically to stay in the selected language.
**dsh-language-guard** 的功能「提示词语言约束」：在系统提示词的首段和末段加入目标语言规则，强化档还会在工具说明后重申。
**dsh-language-guard** 的功能「语言选择」：可自动跟随界面语言或手动指定 BCP-47 标签，并支持会话内 `/language` 临时覆盖。
**dsh-language-guard** 的功能「周期提醒」：周期档在设定轮次的首个步骤加入语言自检提醒，可配置 3–50 轮间隔。
**dsh-language-guard** 的功能「网页设置和快速切换」：在插件设置卡片配置规则，并从侧栏菜单切换自动模式或常用语言。

dsh-language-guard README · Why you need it：The DSH system prompt is assembled from many sections: identity, plan policy, team policy, **tool descriptions**, deliverable references, deployment persona. The largest block by far is the tool documentation — written in English, and placed in the middle of the prompt.

dsh-language-guard README · Why you need it：Measured on DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 (everything after order 50): **98.1% of the characters and 99.8% of the ASCII** come from English tool documentation, and 5.7K–14K characters separate the opening section from the closing one. The model reads overwhelmingly English tokens, and so it drifts:

dsh-language-guard README · Why you need it：A single "please answer in Chinese" line at the very top of the system prompt is enough for a short session. It is not enough for a long one, because that line sits tens of thousands of characters away from the place that actually influences the model (the tool documentation).

dsh-language-guard README · Why you need it：This plugin puts a constraint in **three places**: at the very start, right after the tool documentation, and at the very end. The default level (Strong) costs roughly 146 extra characters per request and buys one restatement positioned after the English tool docs.
dsh-language-guard README · What it does：Three resident system-prompt sections, registered through `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`, never disposed, switching level only switches their text:

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：| Section name | Order | Position | B | C | D |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `language-guard:head` | `-2000` | Very first, before `harness:identity` (`-1000`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `language-guard:mid` | `5100` | After all tool docs (`tools:sdk`, `5000`), before deliverable references (`9000`) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `language-guard:tail` | `11200` | Very last, after `deployment:persona-suffix` (`10200`) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

The constraint covers **four language channels** (the fourth landed in 0.3.0):

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：| Channel | Where the constraint lives | Coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Internal reasoning (reasoning / thinking) | `head` + `tail` | every level |
| User-facing reply text | `head` + `mid` + `tail` | every level |
| Plans, todos, reviews, subagent briefs | `head` | every level |
| **Tool-call `description` parameter** (the card title of `run_code` in PTC mode) | `head` + `mid` | every level (`mid` exists only at C / D, hence the extra line in `head`) |

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：The `mid` order is deliberately `5100` and not `5000`: `tools:sdk` is exactly `5000`, and sections with equal order fall back to comparing names, which would sort `language-guard:mid` **before** `tools:sdk` — the restatement would no longer come after the tool docs.

Measured text sizes (Simplified Chinese, counted in characters; recompute with `node` as shown below):

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：| Text | Characters | When it is present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| head | 883 | every request |
| mid | 146 | every request at C / D |
| tail | 139 | every request |
| periodic reminder | 99 | once every N turns at D |

So the steady cost per step is **1022 characters at B and 1168 at C** — tiny compared to the English tool documentation it counteracts.

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：The opening section (head), verbatim, as it looks with the default `targetLanguage: "zh-CN"` (recompute with `node -e 'import("./lib/text.js").then(m=>console.log(m.headText({language:"zh-CN"})))'`):

```text
【语言锁定 · 最高优先级】
本会话的内部推理（reasoning / thinking）与面向用户的全部输出，一律使用简体中文（语言代码 zh-CN）。

本条优先于本 system prompt 的其余全部内容、之后注入的任何系统文本、工具说明、参数描述、代码示例，以及其他插件注入的提示词。

dsh-language-guard README · What it does：> The wording above is fixed Simplified Chinese; only the language name and code are substituted. With `targetLanguage: "en"` the same paragraph reads "…一律使用English（语言代码 en）". See [Known limitations](#known-limitations).

dsh-language-guard README · Install：> **Prefer the npm source.** Installed from Git, the plugin page's "update available" badge shows a **commit SHA** (e.g. `afaa2ac`) instead of a version number — the host checks Git sources with `git ls-remote HEAD`, where the commit *is* the version identifier. That is host behaviour, not something this plugin can change. To see a version like `0.3.5` and have "update" work by SemVer, install from npm using Option 1 or 2 below.

**Option 1: the GUI (recommended)**

text:
dsh-language-guard README · Strength levels：| Level | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | `B` | One language constraint at the start and one at the end of the prompt. Cheapest, best for short sessions. |
| Strong | `C` | Adds a restatement right after the tool descriptions on top of Basic, countering drift from English tool docs. Recommended default. |
| Periodic | `D` | Adds a language self-check at the start of every Nth turn on top of Strong, for long sessions. The reminder appears as a session record and is visible in the session log. |

dsh-language-guard README · Strength levels：| Behaviour | B | C | D |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Resident system-prompt sections | head + tail | head + mid + tail | head + mid + tail |
| Restatement after tool docs | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Self-check every N turns | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (N defaults to 8, range 3–50) |
| New record in the session log | none | none | one per N turns (`source.kind = "language-guard"`) |
| Injection timing | — | — | the **first step** of a matching turn, alongside that turn's user message; no extra request |
| Counter after restart / resume | — | — | **not reset**: the turn number comes from the session log's `turn` projection, so `turn % N` is stable |
| Best for | short sessions, token-sensitive | the default | long sessions, or drift already observed |

dsh-language-guard README · Strength levels：- **Start with the default, Strong.** It is the only level aimed at the actual root cause (English tool docs), and it costs about 146 characters per step.
- **Short sessions, or every token counts** → drop to **Basic**. Start and end constraints are enough for a 3–5 turn session.
- **Sessions that run dozens of turns, or you have already seen reasoning slide back into English** → raise to **Periodic**. Smaller N means more frequent reminders; the default 8 is a compromise. N = 3 is noisy.
dsh-language-guard README · Configuration：Seven fields, all `volatile` (a change takes effect immediately — no restart, no plugin remount):

dsh-language-guard README · Configuration：| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `languageMode` | `"" \| "auto" \| "manual"` | `""` | tri-state enum, case-sensitive | Language mode. `"auto"` follows the interface language, `"manual"` pins `targetLanguage`, `""` means "never chosen" and is resolved by the migration rule below |
| `targetLanguage` | `string` | `"zh-CN"` | a valid BCP-47 tag (`/^[A-Za-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{2,8})*$/`) | Target language. `zh-CN` Simplified Chinese, `zh-TW` Traditional Chinese, `en` English, `ja` Japanese, `ko` Korean; any other valid tag is used as-is |
| `strength` | `"B" \| "C" \| "D"` | `"C"` | enum, case-sensitive | Strength level, see above |
| `injectEveryNRounds` | `number` | `8` | 3–50, integer | How often the Periodic self-check is added. Only used at D; the control is disabled at other levels |
| `preserveCodeTerms` | `boolean` | `true` | `true` / `false` | `true`: code, commands, paths, identifiers, API fields and raw error text stay verbatim. `false`: technical terms are preferred in the target language, with the English term in parentheses when needed |
| `extraRules` | `string` | `""` | any text |

dsh-language-guard README · Configuration：The `targetLanguage` → display name mapping is fixed (no language guessing): `zh-CN` / `zh-Hans` / `zh-SG` → 简体中文, `zh-TW` / `zh-HK` / `zh-MO` / `zh-Hant` → 繁體中文, `en` / `en-US` / `en-GB` → English, `ja` / `ja-JP` → 日本語, `ko` / `ko-KR` → 한국어; any other valid tag is displayed as the code itself.

dsh-language-guard README · Configuration：Configuration lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. **A patch replaces `config` wholesale — it does not deep-merge** — so a manual override must restate every field, otherwise the omitted ones are lost:

```yaml
- id: dsh-language-guard
  name: dsh-language-guard
  config:
    languageMode: auto

dsh-language-guard README · Automatic language mode：`languageMode` decides where the target language comes from:

| Mode | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto** | The target language follows the DSH **interface language**. Switch the UI to English and the next message gets an English constraint |
| **Manual** | The target language is pinned to `targetLanguage`, regardless of the interface language |

dsh-language-guard README · Automatic language mode：**Auto is the default.** A fresh install needs no configuration: a Simplified Chinese UI constrains Simplified Chinese, an English UI constrains English.

dsh-language-guard README · Resolution order：Auto mode has exactly two sources, taken in order:

1. **The interface language** (`preference` in the `locale` configuration) — the `Settings → General → Language` setting.
2. **The `targetLanguage` value** (default `zh-CN`) — the fallback when the interface language is unavailable.

Mapping (`zh`-prefixed tags → `zh-CN`, `en`-prefixed tags → `en`, any other valid tag is kept as-is):

dsh-language-guard README · Resolution order：| Interface language | Target language | The constraint reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zh` / `zh-CN` / `zh-Hans` | `zh-CN` | 简体中文 |
| `en` / `en-US` | `en` | English |
| `ja` | `ja` | 日本語 |
| `ko` | `ko` | 한국어 |
| any other valid BCP-47 | as-is | that language's display name or code |

dsh-language-guard README · Resolution order：> **Why is there no "system language" step?** The Host half runs as an `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` child process: `require("electron")` throws `Cannot find module 'electron'`, and `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale` always returns `en-US`, which would misclassify Chinese users as English speakers. **There is no reliable system-language signal on the Host side**, so the plugin neither guesses nor fabricates one.

dsh-language-guard README · Upgrading from 0.1.x：If you had picked a `targetLanguage` by hand (say `ja`) and never touched `languageMode`, you stay in **manual** mode after the upgrade — the interface language never silently overrides your choice. The rule: `languageMode` empty **and** `targetLanguage` different from the default `zh-CN` → manual.

Pick "Auto" in the settings card to follow the interface language instead. Once you have chosen explicitly, the migration rule never applies again.

dsh-language-guard README · Seeing what it resolved to：The first control group in the settings card is the language mode; with "Auto" selected it spells out the current result and its source right below:

```text
Currently resolved to 简体中文
from the interface language
```

dsh-language-guard README · Seeing what it resolved to：When the source line says "from the interface language" it means the interface language **you explicitly picked in DSH settings**; if you never picked one it says "interface language not detected, using the configured value" rather than guessing from the browser or the OS — the Host and the settings card read the same value (`preference` of the `locale` namespace in `settings.describe()`), so what the panel shows is exactly what gets injected. The sidebar quick-switch button label shows the same state, e.g. "Auto, 简体中文".

dsh-language-guard README · Seeing what it resolved to：**Changing the interface language needs no restart**: the plugin caches it on startup and subscribes to `settings/document-updated` (refreshing when the `locale` namespace changes), so the very next system-prompt assembly uses the new value.

dsh-language-guard README · Settings panel：Path: **sidebar Plugins → installed plugins → `dsh-language-guard`**. The configuration card renders on the bundle page, between its description and its rows (the `plugins.bundle.config` slot, keyed by the package name). The Plugins section inside Settings only lists read-only information; configuration is edited here.

The card, top to bottom:

dsh-language-guard README · Settings panel：1. **Language mode** — two radios, Auto / Manual. With Auto selected it spells out "currently resolved to X" plus the source (interface language / configured value), and follows the interface language when you change it. In Auto mode the target-language control in item 3 is disabled.
2. **Strength** — three radio rows (`fieldset` + same-named `radio`), all three descriptions visible side by side, with a "Recommended" badge on C. A radio group rather than a `<select>`, because the differences have to be comparable at a glance.
3. **Injection interval (turns)** — a number input, 3–50, disabled with an explanation outside the Periodic level.
4. **Target language** — a text field plus five preset chips (简体中文 / 繁體中文 / English / 日本語 / 한국어). Custom tags go straight into the field; it validates as you type and disables Save while invalid.
5. **Keep code and technical terms verbatim** — a switch (`role="switch"` + `aria-checked`).
6. **Additional rules** — a textarea with a local draft and Save / Discard changes.
7. **Override the opening rules (advanced)** — collapsed by default. Editing it replaces the highest-priority constraint outright, so it

dsh-language-guard README · Settings panel：Every field has a "Reset to default" action (clears the user value back to the schema default).

The saved state reads "Saved · no restart needed, applies to the next message". Level, switch and interval are written on change; text fields use a draft plus an explicit Save so that typing does not write to disk on every keystroke.
dsh-language-guard README · Quick language switch：At the foot of the sidebar, next to Settings (the `sidebar.footer.action` slot, `id = "language-guard"`, `order = 100`):

dsh-language-guard README · Quick language switch：- Sidebar wide: icon + the language's own name + `▾`.
- Sidebar collapsed to a 56px rail: icon only, with a complete `aria-label`.
- Clicking opens a dropdown menu (not a cycle). The first entry is **Auto** (follow the interface language), followed by the five presets. The current entry is checked; in Auto mode the button label reads "Auto, X" and the Auto entry spells out "Currently auto-resolved to X". When the current value is not one of the five presets the raw code is shown with nothing checked.
- Keyboard: Enter / Space opens, Escape closes and returns focus, ↑↓ moves through the menu.
- A hint at the bottom of the menu points to the settings text field for other languages.

dsh-language-guard README · Quick language switch：Picking an entry writes the configuration immediately, and the sidebar label and the settings text field stay in sync both ways. Once the write settles, a line appears above the button for four seconds: "已保存 · 无需重启，下一条消息即生效" when the language actually changed, "当前已是 X" when the entry you picked was already the current one (so a click is never a silent no-op), and the failure reason when the write is rejected.

dsh-language-guard README · Quick language switch：> **Changing the configuration does not require restarting DSH.** Writes go through `dsh-config-editor`, which applies them through the Loader right after touching the disk; volatile fields replace the running references without remounting the plugin (`cordis-plugin-loader`'s `_commitVolatile` → `loader/volatile-update`), and the system prompt is re-assembled on every request, so **your next message** already carries the new language. Only **changing the plugin's code** (for example upgrading the version) needs a restart — not a configuration change.

dsh-language-guard README · The `/language` slash command：A shortcut from the composer. It only sets an in-memory override for this run — **it does not write configuration**, so a restart returns to the configured value:

```text
/language          report the current language and the configured value
/language ja       switch to Japanese for this run
/language reset    clear the override, back to the configured value
/language default  same as reset
dsh-language-guard README · The `/language` slash command：An invalid tag returns an error and changes nothing. The override wins over configuration: `override > configured value > default`.

dsh-language-guard README · Verifying that the constraint reached the system prompt：Levels, panels and switches are all just claims until you look at what the model actually received. DSH records every request's system prompt as a `system/message` event in the session log (`~/.dsh/sessions/<escaped working directory>/<session id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd`). The three steps below reproduce anywhere the plugin is installed.
section: Verifying that the constraint reached the system prompt

2. Switch Strength from Strong to Periodic.
3. The footer reads "Saved · no restart needed, applies to the next message".

echo "$latest"

3. Print each system node's length and check whether the three sections are present

text: dsh-language-guard README · 3. Print each system node's length and check whether the three sections are present：At Strong (or Periodic) you should see `sections=3/3`.
section: 3. Print each system node's length and check whether the three sections are present

text:
dsh-language-guard README · Step 3: switch to Basic and watch the middle section disappear：1. Switch Strength to Basic and send another message.
2. Re-run the command from step 2.

The new system node should report `sections=2/3` — the missing one is `【语言锁定 · 中段重申】` — and its length should be **146 characters shorter** than the previous node, exactly the size of the mid section (see [What it does](#what-it-does)). At Basic, `language-guard:mid` returns an empty string, and `renderPrompt` filters empty text out, so no empty section or stray blank line is left behind.
section: Step 3: switch to Basic and watch the middle section disappear

text:
dsh-language-guard README · Extra checks：- **The Periodic reminder**: set Strength to Periodic and the interval to 3, then chat for 3 turns. The session log gains `user/message` events whose `data.message.source.kind` is `"language-guard"`, `form` is `"notice"` and `summary` is `"语言自检"`. In the UI it renders as a collapsed line reading "上下文注入 · language-guard · 语言自检" — it never impersonates a user turn.
- **Subagents are skipped**: at Periodic, dispatch a subagent; its session log contains no record with `source.kind = "language-guard"` (a subagent inherits the parent's system-prompt constraint, and its compact context is left alone).
- **Switching language**: pick 日本語 from the sidebar menu, send a message, and the new system node reads "一律使用日本語（语言代码 ja）".
- **Disabling the plugin**: with the plugin disabled there are no sections and no injections; the new system node reports `sections=0/3`. That is a clean fallback, not a leftover.

dsh-language-guard README · One-command check：The manual steps above collapse into a single command:

```bash
node scripts/verify-installed.mjs
```

It locates the most recently written session log, decompresses it, reports the length and section hits of every `system/message` node, and prints two verdicts: **whether a legacy dsh-context promptPrefix/promptSuffix is still present**, and **whether this plugin is in effect**. An explicit path also works:

dsh-language-guard README · One-command check：```bash
node scripts/verify-installed.mjs ~/.dsh/sessions/<project>/<session>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd
```

Requires the `zstd` command on your PATH (macOS: `brew install zstd`).

dsh-language-guard README · Coexisting with dsh-context：The third-party plugin `dsh-context` registers `promptPrefix` / `promptSuffix` sections whose order values **collide exactly** with this plugin's (`-2000` and `11200`).

dsh-language-guard README · Coexisting with dsh-context：- **Nothing breaks**: sorting is `order - order || compareNames(name)`, so a shared order is not a shared name. `"dsh-context:prompt-prefix" < "language-guard:head"` (`d` < `l`), so dsh-context's two sections stably sort before this plugin's.
- **But it burns tokens twice**: both are writing a language constraint into the same place — the same idea, twice.
- **Recommendation**: after installing this plugin, clear `dsh-context`'s `promptPrefix` / `promptSuffix`, or disable `dsh-context` outright.

dsh-language-guard README · Coexisting with dsh-context：A permanent hint sits at the bottom of the settings card, and `meta.description` in both `locale/{zh,en}.json` carries the same sentence. This plugin **does not detect or rewrite** `dsh-context`'s configuration — writing another plugin's config violates least surprise.

dsh-language-guard README · How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-cot-translation` (together with `cot-translation-bundle`) is an official experimental plugin that does **rendering-layer translation**: it machine-translates the expanded reasoning shown in the UI into another language. Its own README states that translation sends the displayed reasoning to the selected external service, which may include private code or conversation details, and that the original reasoning remains in the session and model context.
section: How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin

text: dsh-language-guard README · How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin：This plugin does **generation-layer constraint**: it tells the model, in the system prompt, to think and answer in the language you chose.
section: How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin

text:
dsh-language-guard README · How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin：| | cot-translation | dsh-language-guard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Acts on | reasoning text already rendered in the UI | the model's next generation |
| Layer | Client rendering (`conversation.chat.reasoning.body` slot) | Host system prompt (`ctx.systemPrompt.section()`) |
| Network | yes, sends text to an external translation service | no, zero network requests |
| Reads conversation content | yes, ships the reasoning body out | no, only writes its own constraint sections |
| Language of the original reasoning | unchanged (still in the session and context) | the language you configured |
section: How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin

text: dsh-language-guard README · How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin：The two are **complementary, not competing**: one decides what language the model thinks in, the other decides what language that thinking is displayed in. They can be installed together — but if this plugin already pins thinking to Simplified Chinese, pointing cot-translation at Simplified Chinese adds nothing; its useful setting is the opposite direction (model thinks in Chinese, you read it in English).
section: How it differs from the official cot-translation plugin

text:
dsh-language-guard README · Known limitations：- **The constraint wording is fixed Simplified Chinese.** Only the language name and code are substituted, so with `targetLanguage: "en"` the injected text reads "…一律使用English（语言代码 en）". Models handle this fine, but the prose is not localized. Localizing the templates is a future change.
- **The Periodic reminder is visible in the chat UI**, collapsed into one line reading "上下文注入 · language-guard · 语言自检". The English identifier `language-guard` **cannot be hidden** — the client renders `source.kind` verbatim as the injection label, exactly as it does for the official `agent-instructions` and `skill-invocation`. Localizing it would require a custom `conversation.chat.node` renderer for the context node; the first release does not do that.
- **The Client half has no turn counter**, so the panel cannot show "the next injection lands on turn X".
- **The quick switch menu lists five presets plus one "Custom" entry.** Custom BCP-47 tags must be typed into the settings field; in Manual mode with a value outside the presets, the menu gains a checked "Custom: <language>" entry so that six unchecked rows no longer look like "nothing was ever set"
dsh-language-guard README · Design boundaries：This plugin deliberately does **not** do the following — each would either break host conventions or make debugging impossible:

dsh-language-guard README · Design boundaries：- It does not listen to `system-prompt/assemble` to add or remove host text; it only declares its own sections through `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`.
- It does not rewrite `llm/stream` reasoning deltas — it never fabricates "thinking".
- It does not touch decision fields other than `messages` in `agent/pre-step`, and it appends no new event types; the Periodic path returns `{ ...decision, messages }`, preserving `startsRequestSeries` and the rest.
- It makes no network requests, reads no conversation content, reports nothing.
- `dependencies` is empty; the Client half only `require('react')` from the host module table.
- The constraint text is stable within a session, avoiding frequent in-history replacement and prompt-cache invalidation.
